extracted.intended_audience: ML/AI conference reviewers (industry and academic researchers) preparing peer reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, actionable guidance for conducting thorough peer reviews of ML/AI conference submissions, covering a two-phase workflow (deep reading then clear feedback), markup conventions, and elements that good reviews often miss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deep Reading Phase (1–2 hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deep Reading Phase (1–2 hours) — maintain curiosity and openness while engaging the paper's content and methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spend 1–2 hours reading with curiosity and openness; focus on understanding the paper's content, methods, and claims. Use markup while reading to capture immediate reactions and questions. The aim is comprehension rather than quick judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear Feedback Phase (1–4 hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear Feedback Phase (1–4 hours) — turn margin notes into coherent, actionable commentary without rushing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate 1–4 hours to convert margin annotations into organized, actionable review text. Synthesize points, prioritize major weaknesses, and avoid rushing this stage so recommendations are constructive and implementable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markup strategy — color-coded annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Color-coded annotation: Green — contributions and positive elements. Blue / neutral — general understanding, questions, content feedback. Red — grammar and language issues, kept separate from substantive critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use distinct colors to separate praise, substantive questions/feedback, and grammar/language issues. Keep red (grammar/language) separate from substantive critique so authors and chairs can distinguish writing polish from technical/scientific issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close reading indication via margin markup
rubrics_metrics.description: "If you don't have any markup in the margins for about half of a page, you probably did not read closely enough."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use frequent margin notes while reading. A lack of annotations across half a page likely indicates insufficient close reading; aim to mark contributions, confusions, and issues regularly to show engagement and support later feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score-improvement pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify what revisions would strengthen the rating (weak reject → weak accept → strong accept).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each major weakness, explain concrete changes that would move the paper to higher decision categories. Tie suggested fixes to the scoring rubric so authors and area chairs can see how revisions change the recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curiosity / open comments (non-scored)
rubrics_metrics.description: Curiosity / open comments — non-scored section for exploratory ideas and questions; fosters collaborative dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a separate, non-scored section for speculative ideas, follow-up questions, or exploratory suggestions. This encourages constructive engagement and can surface promising directions without affecting the score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about confusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency about confusion — request clarification rather than penalizing unclear content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parts of the paper are unclear, explicitly state what is confusing and ask for clarification instead of immediately downgrading. Differentiate between problems of exposition and substantive flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number feedback points by section
rubrics_metrics.description: Number feedback points (i1, i2, …) by section for easier author response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize critiques into numbered items, optionally prefixed by section (e.g., i1, s3:i2). This makes it easier for authors to respond point-by-point and for area chairs to track major vs. minor issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit reviews after completion to synthesize key weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Edit reviews after completion to synthesize key weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After drafting, re-read and consolidate: emphasize the top 2–3 major concerns, remove redundant points, and ensure the review clearly communicates the principal reasons for the score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use shorter templates for clear accepts/rejects; reserve detail for borderlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Use shorter templates for clear accepts/rejects; reserve detailed reviews for borderline or award-nomination papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save reviewer effort by writing concise justifications for obvious accepts/rejects; invest more time in detailed, constructive feedback for borderline submissions or those you consider for awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a supportive tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt supportive tone rather than adversarial positioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write feedback to help authors improve; avoid adversarial or punitive language. A constructive tone increases the likelihood authors can act on suggestions and reduces unproductive conflict.
